text: Gratiam et pacem a Deo Patre nostro, et Domino Jesu Christo.
note: *Grātiam* keeps its capital: the greeting is its own sentence after the address of 1:1, as settled Rom 1:7, 1 Cor 1:3 and 2 Cor 1:2; *Patre* capital, God the Father (θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν; decision 20; *nostrō* lower case), as the same greeting in 2 Cor 1:2 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Concelebrandus Deus et Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi, qui nos felicitavit omni ubertate divina in rebus Christi caelestibus:
note: *Pater* capital, God the Father (decision 20; NRSV \"the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ\"), as settled 2 Cor 1:3 *Deus et Pater Dominī nostrī* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: ut Domini nostri Jesu Christi Deus, gloriae Pater, vos sapientiae et patefactionis auctore Spiritu donet, quo eum cognoscatis.
note: *Pater* capital: *glōriæ Pater* is God (ὁ πατὴρ τῆς δόξης; NRSV \"the Father of glory\"; decision 20). *Spīritū* keeps the draft's capital: Castellio makes the Spirit the giver (*sapientiæ et patefactiōnis auctōre Spīritū*, with the Spirit, the author of wisdom and revelation), though the NRSV has \"a spirit of wisdom\" (an uncertain call). *ut* lower case: 1:16 ends without punctuation (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: (quae ejus corpus est) dedit caput complementum omnia complentis in omnibus.
note: *quæ* lower case inside the parenthesis: a relative clause on *ecclēsiæ* (1:22) in the middle of the sentence (ἥτις ἐστὶ τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ), as settled 1 Cor 1:6 *(quemadmodum …)* and Exod 19:5 *(nam …)*; 1:22 ends with a comma (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Verum Deus, misericordia dives, tanta nos caritate complexus est,
note: a new paragraph, as the BSB's ordinary break: 2:3 ends a sentence and *Vērum Deus* turns from the readers' former death to God's mercy (2:4–10), the step the BSB and NRSV mark (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: ut quum delictis essemus mortui, revocaverit nos in vitam una cum Christo (estis beneficio servati)
note: a space before the parenthesis (the draft had none); *ut* lower case: 2:4 ends with a comma (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quamobrem mementote, vos aliquando carne alienigenas (qui praeputium vocamini ab ea, quae circumcisio dicitur, in corpore manu facta)
note: a space before the parenthesis (the draft had none) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: In quo vos quoque una aedificamini, ad Dei domicilium, divino adflatu.
note: *dīvīnō afflātū* lower case, as 1573 (*diuino afflatu*, canvas 895) and every *dīvīnō afflātū* in the settled books (Matt 22:43, Acts 20:22, 1 Cor 12:3): Castellio's phrase for ἐν πνεύματι, an adjective and a common noun, not the name *Spīritus* (decision 20). *In quō* keeps its capital after 2:21's colon, as the settled books do after a colon (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: et omnibus perspicuum faciam, quae sit mysterii communio, quod ab omni aeternitate apud Deum (qui omnia per Jesum Christum condidit) fuit celatum,
note: a space before the parenthesis (the draft had none); *et* lower case: 3:8 ends with a comma (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Huius gratia flecto mea genua ad Patrem Domini nostri Jesu Christi,
note: *Patrem* capital, God the Father (πρὸς τὸν πατέρα τοῦ Κυρίου; NRSV \"before the Father\"; decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Ei vero, qui ea vi, quae viget in nobis, potest omnia longe longeque copiosius facere, quam nos poscere aut cogitare,
note: a new paragraph, as the BSB's ordinary break: 3:19 ends the prayer with a full stop and *Eī vērō* opens the doxology (3:20–21), as the NRSV sets it (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Unus Deus et Pater omnium, qui est supra omnia, et per omnia, et in omnibus.
note: *Pater* capital, God the Father (εἷς Θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ πάντων; NRSV \"one God and Father of all\"; decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Ceterum unicuique nostrum collatum est beneficium, pro portione doni Christi.
note: a new paragraph, as the BSB's ordinary break: 4:6 ends the list of the one body, Spirit, Lord and God, and *Cēterum ūnīcuique nostrum* turns to the gifts given to each (4:7–16) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Itaque \\q1 \\qt “Adscendens in sublime (inquit ille)\\qt* \\q2 \\qt captivos abduxit,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et dona dedit hominibus.”\\qt*
note: Ps 68:18 after *Itaque* (Διὸ λέγει), with *(inquit ille)* inside the marks as settled Rom 14:11 *(inquit Dominus)* and Acts 2:17 *(inquit Deus)*: in \\qt with “…”, as poetry in three lines after the BSB (*Ascendēns in sublīme* / *captīvōs abdūxit,* / *et dōna dedit hominibus*); *Ascendēns* capital as the quotation's first word; no colon added after *Itaque* (1573 has none), which is Paul's and outside the marks (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quid est autem “adscendit,” nisi quod prius in imas terrae partes descenderat?
note: prose again after the poetry of 4:8 (`m`; the BSB's break); *“ascendit,”* is the quotation's word named, not spoken (Τὸ δέ, Ἀνέβη; BSB What does “He ascended” mean), so in quotation marks as words named (decision 39), lower case, the comma inside as 2 Cor 1:18 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: donec perveniamus omnes ad unitatem fidei, cognitionisque Filii Dei, in virum adultum, ad modum plenae aetatis christianae:
note: *Fīliī* capital, the Son of God (τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ; decision 20), as settled 2 Cor 1:19 *Fīlius* and 1 Cor 1:9 *Fīliī*; *chrīstiānæ* lower case, an adjective (as settled Rom 15:29); *dōnec* lower case: 4:12 ends with a comma (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: ex quo totum corpus omnibus (per quas efficitur administratio) commissuris compactum atque connexum, actione (quae pro cujusque partis modo fit) facit corporis incrementum, ad semet exstruendum in caritate.
note: a space before both parentheses (the draft had none); *ex* lower case: 4:15 ends with a comma (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: At vos non ita Christum didicistis,
note: a new paragraph, as the BSB's ordinary break: 4:19 ends the picture of the Gentiles with a full stop, and *At vōs nōn ita* turns to the readers (4:20–24), a new step in the NRSV as in the BSB (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: veterem hominem (qui superiores vestri fuere mores) deponere, qui fallacibus perit cupiditatibus,
note: a space before the parenthesis (the draft had none); *veterem* lower case: 4:21 ends with a comma (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: et mentis vestrae spiritu renovari,
note: *spīritū* lower case: the human spirit, \"the spirit of your minds\" (τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ νοὸς ὑμῶν; NRSV and BSB lower case), not the Holy Spirit (decision 20); 1573 *spiritu*; *et* lower case: 4:22 ends with a comma (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quamobrem deposita falsitate, loquimini vera alius cum alio: quandoquidem alii aliorum membra sumus.
note: a new paragraph, as the BSB's ordinary break: 4:24 ends the old self and the new with a full stop, and *Quamobrem dēpositā falsitāte* opens the particular commands that follow from it (4:25–32). Zech 8:16 (*loquiminī vēra …*) is woven into the command and left unmarked, as the BSB leaves it (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Hoc enim scitote, nullum scortatorem, aut impurum, aut avarum (qui est deastricola) habiturum esse hereditatem in Christi Deique regno.
note: a space before the parenthesis (the draft had none) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Propterea, \\q1 \\qt “Expergiscere, qui dormis (inquit)\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et surge ex mortuis,\\qt* \\q2 \\qt et tibi Christus adfulgebit.”\\qt*
note: the saying after *Proptereā … (inquit)* (Διὸ λέγει, the formula of 4:8), which the BSB sets as poetry in three lines: in \\qt with “…”, *(inquit)* inside the marks as 4:8 and Rom 14:11; *Expergīscere* capital as the quotation's first word, as 1573 prints it (*Propterea, Expergiscere qui dormis (inquit)*, canvas 896); *Proptereā* is Paul's, outside. Its source is uncertain (Isa 60:1 and 26:19, or a hymn), but the formula is the one Paul uses for Scripture at 4:8 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Videte igitur, ut solerter gradiamini, non ut insipientes, sed ut sapientes;
note: prose again after the poetry of 5:14, as a new paragraph (the BSB's b m): *Vidēte igitur* draws the conclusion and opens the call to walk wisely (5:15–21) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Neve inebriamini vino, in quo inest luxuria: sed Spiritu pleni este,
note: *Spīritū* capital: \"be filled with the Spirit\" (πληροῦσθε ἐν πνεύματι; NRSV and BSB capital; decision 20); 1573 *spiritu* (it capitalizes none). *Nēve* keeps its capital after 5:17's colon, as the settled books do after a colon (1 Cor 41 : 1, Rom 54 : 1) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Deo et Patri semper pro omnibus gratias agentes in nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi:
note: *Patrī* capital, God the Father (τῷ Θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ; NRSV \"to God the Father\"; decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Alius alii obedientes cum Dei metu.
note: the draft's paragraph (the BSB's heading) moved to 5:22: *Alius aliī obēdientēs* is the last participle of the sentence begun at 5:18 (*plēnī este … colloquentēs … canentēs … agentēs … obēdientēs*), and 5:20 ends with a colon; as decision 28 moved the BSB's paragraphs off mid-sentence in Mark. *Alius* keeps its capital after the colon (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Vos uxores, vestris parete viris, ut Domino.
note: the paragraph moved here from 5:21 (above), also the BSB's ordinary break: 5:21 ends with a full stop and *Vōs uxōrēs* opens the household rules with their first address (5:22–33) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Nam vir caput uxoris est, ut Christus ecclesiae caput, idemque corporis Servator est.
note: *Servātor* capital: Christ is the Saviour of the body (αὐτὸς σωτήρ τοῦ σώματος; NRSV \"the Savior\"), and decision 20 names *Servātor* among the titles capitalized for Christ, as the settled *Servātōrem* (4); a predicate, but a title, not a relation like 2 Cor 6:18 *pater erō* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Vos viri, amate vestras uxores, ut Christus amavit ecclesiam, seque pro ea dedidit,
note: a new paragraph, as the BSB's ordinary break: 5:24 ends with a full stop and *Vōs virī* turns to the husbands, the second address of the household rules (as 5:22, 6:1, 6:4, 6:5, 6:9) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: \\qt “Propterea homo, relicto patre atque matre, adhaerebit uxori suae, fietque ex duobus una caro.”\\qt*
note: Gen 2:24 (the BSB quotes it) in \\qt with “…”, prose as the BSB; no formula here (as the Greek, ἀντὶ τούτου), so the quotation stands as its own sentence with *Proptereā* capital as its first word, as settled 2 Cor 13:1 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: \\qt “Honora tuum patrem atque matrem,”\\qt* quod primum est cum promissione praeceptum,
note: the commandment (Exod 20:12; Deut 5:16) in \\qt with “…”, prose as the BSB, which quotes 6:2a and 6:3; *quod prīmum est cum prōmissiōne præceptum* is Paul's comment, outside the marks (the BSB's parenthesis); the words of settled Mark 7:10 *Honōrā tuum patrem atque mātrem* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: \\qt “ut tibi bene sit, et vivas in terra diu.”\\qt*
note: the commandment's promise, reopened after Paul's comment in 6:2 and closed here, as the BSB; *ut* lower case, the sentence runs on from 6:2's comma (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Vos patres, ne vestros irritate natos, sed eos in Domini disciplina ac monitis educate.
note: a new paragraph, as the BSB's ordinary break: 6:3 ends with a full stop and *Vōs patrēs* turns from the children to the fathers, a new address (as 5:22, 5:25, 6:5, 6:9) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Item vos domini, vices eis reddite, remissis minis, scientes, eorum et vestrum Dominum in caelis esse, qui nihil personis tribuat.
note: a new paragraph, as the BSB's ordinary break: 6:8 ends with a full stop and *Item vōs dominī* turns from the slaves to the masters, a new address (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Item salutis galeam sumite, et gladium Spiritus, hoc est, divina dicta,
note: *Spīritūs* capital: \"the sword of the Spirit\" (τὴν μάχαιραν τοῦ πνεύματος; NRSV and BSB capital; decision 20); 1573 *spiritus* (it capitalizes none) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Pacem fratribus et caritatem cum fiducia opto a Deo Patre, et Domino Jesu Christo.
note: *Patre* capital, God the Father (ἀπὸ Θεοῦ πατρὸς; decision 20), as 1:2 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Adsit Dei gratia immortalis omnibus, Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum amantibus: Amen. \\cls Ad Ephesios missa est Roma per Tychicum.
note: the subscription set apart as \\cls after the verse (decision 37), as 1573 prints it under the blessing (*amantibus : Amen . Ad Ephesios missa est Roma per Tichicum*, canvas 897) and as Rom 16:27, 1 Cor 16:24, 2 Cor 13:14; the colon before *Āmēn* kept, as 1573 and the draft (Claude, 2026-11-11)
